<section id="GeneralBodyContent">
<div class="content rte-content">
<p>Rental providers (landlords) and agents must give renters this guide on or before the day they move in. You can read more about renting guides at�<a href="/housing/renting/starting-and-changing-rental-agreements/resources-and-guides-for-renters/resources-and-guides-overview">Resources and guides overview</a>.</p>
<h3>Introduction</h3>
<p>Victoria has some of the strongest rental protections in Australia, but�renting can still be complicated. With 1 in 3 Victorians now renting, understanding your rental rights has never been more important.</p>
<p>The <em>Renters Guide</em> explains the rules and your rights at every stage�of renting in Victoria, from applying for a property to moving out.</p>
<p>Whether you�re a first-time renter or have rented before, this guide�provides you with the information you need to rent confidently.</p>
<h3>Key terms</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Rental provider:</strong>�landlord.</li>
<li><strong>Renter:</strong>�tenant.</li>
<li><strong>Agent:</strong>�real estate agent.</li>
<li><strong>The Residential Tenancies Act 1997:</strong>�This sets out the laws, rights�and responsibilities of renters and rental providers in Victoria.</li>
<li><strong>RTBA:</strong> the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority. It holds residential rental bonds for Victorians as a neutral party, for the renter and the rental provider.</li>
<li><strong>PRBS: </strong>Portable Rental Bond Scheme. Eligible renters can transfer the value of their existing bond or �bond money� to their next rental property, saving them being out of pocket.</li>
<li><strong>RDRV:</strong>�Rental Dispute Resolution Victoria. A free dispute resolution service�to help renters and rental providers resolve disputes.</li>
<li><strong>VCAT:</strong>�Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal. This tribunal resolves�legal disputes and cases in Victoria, including renting issues.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Where to find more information</h3>
<p>Our website has�detailed resources on:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="/housing/renting">General renting information</a>�(for renters, rental providers and agents)</li>
<li><a href="/resources-and-tools/other-languages">Information in other languages</a>�</li>
<li><a href="/resources-and-tools/consumers-with-a-disability/easy-english-factsheets">Easy English resources</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Stay updated</h3>
<p>For the most current information, go to�<a href="/housing/renting">Renting</a>.</p>
<p>Follow Consumer Affairs Victoria on�<a href="https://www.facebook.com/ConsumerAffairsVictoria">Facebook</a>�and�<a href="https://www.instagram.com/consumeraffairsvictoria">Instagram</a>�for regular�renting information and updates.</p>

<h3>Need help in your language?</h3>
<p>Call TIS National interpreting service on <a href="tel: 131 450">131 450</a>.</p>
<p>Ask to be put through to Consumer Affairs Victoria.</p>
